newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH BOND YIELDS FALL, CROWN STABLE VS MARK.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH BOND YIELDS FALL, CROWN STABLE VS MARK.

text.p: Swedish bond yields ended slightly lower on Thursday, helped by international trends, and the crown remained stable against the mark thanks to a Riksbank intervention, dealers said.
Dealers said the debt market felt strong, but James McKay, analyst at PaineWebber, recommended selling long maturities in all European markets, including Sweden.

"The Nordic markets are still vulnerable to a German rate hike, even if I don't think there will be any," he said, adding the Swedish spread to Germany might rise to more than 100 basis points in coming months.
The six-month T-bill rate dropped three basis points to 4.35 percent and the 10-year bond yield fell three to 6.52.
Dealers said the Riksbank bought crowns for mark when the crown was trading around 4.3120 to mark. The Riksbank never comments on interventions.

Some dealers attributed the Riksbank's move, which was the second this week, to the crown's softening against the dollar while others said the central bank merely wanted to smooth out movements in the crown-mark rate in a nervous market.
The crown firmed to 8.0597 against the dollar from 8.0632 late on Wednesday and from 8.10 before the intervention.
The crown also strengthened marginally to 4.2940 against the mark from 4.2910 late Wednesday and from 4.3120 at the time of intervention.
